source.title: Keystone metro cost factor (BLS OEWS wages, see README cost method)

factor.note: MSA 17780 College Station-Bryan, TX: labour index L=0.789, materials M=1.0. 4/5 trades (OEWS May 2024 via O*NET Texas local-wages search extracts). Missing 49-9021: weights renormalised. Ratios to US: 47-2031 0.777; 47-2111 0.799; 47-2152 0.791; 47-2061 0.796. L = 0.789; factor = 0.40*0.789 + 0.60*1.00 = 0.92. M=1.00 (default, no public citable reason to adjust).

cost.method: Factor = 0.40*L + 0.60*M, rounded to 2 decimals. L = weighted mean of (metro annual median wage / US national annual median wage) for SOC 47-2031 Carpenters (0.30), 47-2111 Electricians (0.20), 47-2152 Plumbers/Pipefitters/Steamfitters (0.20), 47-2061 Construction Laborers (0.20), 49-9021 HVAC Mechanics/Installers (0.10), from BLS OEWS; weights renormalised over occupations available for the MSA. M = materials index, 1.00 for all Texas metros (no public citable reason to adjust); qualitative materials notes per MSA. Wave 2 (2026-10-11): all five trades retrieved from O*NET Texas local-wages pages (OEWS May 2024) via search extracts (Secondary); HVAC missing for 28660, 47380, 46340, 17780 (weights renormalised there). provisional removed for every MSA with >=4 trades.

plainLanguage: Since January 1, 2026 College Station uses the newer 2024 residential, energy and plumbing codes and the 2023 electrical code, with local changes. Most new homes are in the GS (General Suburban) district: lots of at least 5,000 sq ft, 25 ft front, 7.5 ft side, 15 ft street-side and 20 ft rear setbacks, up to 2.5 stories / 35 ft. No more than 4 unrelated people may live in one house (only 2 in some overlay neighborhoods), so very large bedroom counts aimed at student renters can be a problem. Some older neighborhoods near Texas A&M have conservation overlays with stricter rules, such as one-story limits. The building permit is about $0.74 per square foot - around $2,100 for a 2,400 sq ft house with garage. Impact fees add roughly $9,600 or more (water, sewer and roads). In a floodplain, the floor must be at least 1 ft above the 100-year flood level.
